title: Biology (B.S.)
summary: An undergraduate map of the science of life, from atoms to the biosphere.

layers.basics: Biology asks how living things work, how they came to be, and how they interact. This track walks from chemistry through cells, genes, evolution, organisms and ecosystems.
layers.deeper: Living things form a hierarchy of levels: atoms, molecules, organelles, cells, tissues, organs, organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems and the biosphere. Every level obeys the same physics and chemistry, yet each is studied with its own questions and methods. Evolution by natural selection and the flow of energy tie the levels together.
layers.expert: Biological explanation works at several levels at once. Proximate questions ask how a mechanism works; ultimate questions ask why natural selection favoured it. Evidence ranges from controlled experiments and sequencing to comparative and historical inference, so statistics and modelling sit beside microscopy and physiology as core skills.
